entries.name: Trapinch
entries.desc: Trapinch’s nest is a sloped, bowl-like pit dug in sand. This Pokémon patiently waits for prey to tumble down the pit. Its giant jaws have enough strength to crush even boulders.

entries.name: Vibrava
entries.desc: To make prey faint, Vibrava generates ultrasonic waves by vigorously making its two wings vibrate. This Pokémon’s ultrasonic waves are so powerful, they can bring on headaches in people.

entries.name: Flygon
entries.desc: Flygon is nicknamed “the elemental spirit of the desert.” Because its flapping wings whip up a cloud of sand, this Pokémon is always enveloped in a sandstorm while flying.

entries.name: Cacnea
entries.desc: Cacnea lives in arid locations such as deserts. It releases a strong aroma from its flower to attract prey. When prey comes near, this Pokémon shoots sharp thorns from its body to bring the victim down.

entries.name: Cacturne
entries.desc: During the daytime, Cacturne remains unmoving so that it does not lose any moisture to the harsh desert sun. This Pokémon becomes active at night when the temperature drops.

entries.name: Swablu
entries.desc: Swablu has light and fluffy wings that are like cottony clouds. This Pokémon is not frightened of people. It lands on the heads of people and sits there like a cotton-fluff hat.

entries.name: Altaria
entries.desc: Altaria dances and wheels through the sky among billowing, cotton-like clouds. By singing melodies in its crystal-clear voice, this Pokémon makes its listeners experience dreamy wonderment.

entries.name: Zangoose
entries.desc: Memories of battling its archrival Seviper are etched into every cell of Zangoose’s body. This Pokémon adroitly dodges attacks with incredible agility.

entries.name: Seviper
entries.desc: Seviper shares a generations-long feud with Zangoose. The scars on its body are evidence of vicious battles. This Pokémon attacks using its sword-edged tail.

entries.name: Lunatone
entries.desc: Lunatone was discovered at a location where a meteoroid fell. As a result, some people theorize that this Pokémon came from space. However, no one has been able to prove this theory so far.

entries.name: Solrock
entries.desc: Solrock is a new species of Pokémon that is said to have fallen from space. It floats in air and moves silently. In battle, this Pokémon releases intensely bright light.

entries.name: Barboach
entries.desc: Barboach’s sensitive whiskers serve as a superb radar system. This Pokémon hides in mud, leaving only its two whiskers exposed while it waits for prey to come along.

entries.name: Whiscash
entries.desc: Whiscash is extremely territorial. Just one of these Pokémon will claim a large pond as its exclusive territory. If a foe approaches it, it thrashes about and triggers a massive earthquake.

entries.name: Corphish
entries.desc: Corphish were originally foreign Pokémon that were imported as pets. They eventually turned up in the wild. This Pokémon is very hardy and has greatly increased its population.

entries.name: Crawdaunt
entries.desc: Crawdaunt has an extremely violent nature that compels it to challenge other living things to battle. Other life-forms refuse to live in ponds inhabited by this Pokémon, making them desolate places.

entries.name: Baltoy
entries.desc: Baltoy moves while spinning around on its one foot. Primitive wall paintings depicting this Pokémon living among people were discovered in some ancient ruins.

entries.name: Claydol
entries.desc: Claydol are said to be dolls of mud made by primitive humans and brought to life by exposure to a mysterious ray. This Pokémon moves about while levitating.

entries.name: Lileep
entries.desc: Lileep became extinct approximately a hundred million years ago. This ancient Pokémon attaches itself to a rock on the seafloor and catches approaching prey using tentacles shaped like flower petals.

entries.name: Cradily
entries.desc: Cradily roams around the ocean floor in search of food. This Pokémon freely extends its tree trunk-like neck and captures unwary prey using its eight tentacles.

entries.name: Anorith
entries.desc: Anorith was regenerated from a prehistoric fossil. This primitive Pokémon once lived in warm seas. It grips its prey firmly between its two large claws.

entries.name: Armaldo
entries.desc: Armaldo’s tough armor makes all attacks bounce off. This Pokémon’s two enormous claws can be freely extended or contracted. They have the power to punch right through a steel slab.

entries.name: Feebas
entries.desc: Feebas’s fins are ragged and tattered from the start of its life. Because of its shoddy appearance, this Pokémon is largely ignored. It is capable of living in both the sea and in rivers.

entries.name: Milotic
entries.desc: Milotic is said to be the most beautiful of all the Pokémon. It has the power to becalm such emotions as anger and hostility to quell bitter feuding.

entries.name: Castform
entries.desc: Castform’s appearance changes with the weather. This Pokémon gained the ability to use the vast power of nature to protect its tiny body.

entries.name: Kecleon
entries.desc: Kecleon is capable of changing its body colors at will to blend in with its surroundings. There is one exception—this Pokémon can’t change the zigzag pattern on its belly.

entries.name: Shuppet
entries.desc: Shuppet is attracted by feelings of jealousy and vindictiveness. If someone develops strong feelings of vengeance, this Pokémon will appear in a swarm and line up beneath the eaves of that person’s home.

entries.name: Banette
entries.desc: Banette generates energy for laying strong curses by sticking pins into its own body. This Pokémon was originally a pitiful plush doll that was thrown away.

entries.name: Duskull
entries.desc: Duskull can pass through any wall no matter how thick it may be. Once this Pokémon chooses a target, it will doggedly pursue the intended victim until the break of dawn.

entries.name: Dusclops
entries.desc: Dusclops’s body is completely hollow—there is nothing at all inside. It is said that its body is like a black hole. This Pokémon will absorb anything into its body, but nothing will ever come back out.

entries.name: Tropius
entries.desc: The bunches of fruit around Tropius’s neck are very popular with children. This Pokémon loves fruit, and eats it continuously. Apparently, its love for fruit resulted in its own outgrowth of fruit.

entries.name: Chimecho
entries.desc: Chimecho makes its cries echo inside its hollow body. When this Pokémon becomes enraged, its cries result in ultrasonic waves that have the power to knock foes flying.

entries.name: Absol
entries.desc: Every time Absol appears before people, it is followed by a disaster such as an earthquake or a tidal wave. As a result, it came to be known as the disaster Pokémon.

entries.name: Wynaut
entries.desc: Wynaut can always be seen with a big, happy smile on its face. Look at its tail to determine if it is angry. When angered, this Pokémon will be slapping the ground with its tail.

entries.name: Snorunt
entries.desc: Snorunt live in regions with heavy snowfall. In seasons without snow, such as spring and summer, this Pokémon steals away to live quietly among stalactites and stalagmites deep in caverns.

entries.name: Glalie
entries.desc: Glalie has a body made of rock, which it hardens with an armor of ice. This Pokémon has the ability to freeze moisture in the atmosphere into any shape it desires.

entries.name: Spheal
entries.desc: Spheal is much faster rolling than walking to get around. When groups of this Pokémon eat, they all clap at once to show their pleasure. Because of this, their mealtimes are noisy.

entries.name: Sealeo
entries.desc: Sealeo has the habit of always juggling on the tip of its nose anything it sees for the first time. This Pokémon occasionally entertains itself by balancing and rolling a Spheal on its nose.

entries.name: Walrein
entries.desc: Walrein’s two massively developed tusks can totally shatter blocks of ice weighing 10 tons with one blow. This Pokémon’s thick coat of blubber insulates it from subzero temperatures.

entries.name: Clamperl
entries.desc: Clamperl’s sturdy shell is not only good for protection—it is also used for clamping and catching prey. A fully grown Clamperl’s shell will be scored with nicks and scratches all over.

entries.name: Huntail
entries.desc: Huntail’s presence went unnoticed by people for a long time because it lives at extreme depths in the sea. This Pokémon’s eyes can see clearly even in the murky dark depths of the ocean.

entries.name: Gorebyss
entries.desc: Gorebyss lives in the southern seas at extreme depths. Its body is built to withstand the enormous pressure of water at incredible depths. Because of this, this Pokémon’s body is unharmed by ordinary attacks.

entries.name: Relicanth
entries.desc: Relicanth is a Pokémon species that existed for a hundred million years without ever changing its form. This ancient Pokémon feeds on microscopic organisms with its toothless mouth.

entries.name: Luvdisc
entries.desc: Luvdisc live in shallow seas in the tropics. This heart-shaped Pokémon earned its name by swimming after loving couples it spotted in the ocean’s waves.

entries.name: Bagon
entries.desc: Bagon has a dream of one day soaring in the sky. In doomed efforts to fly, this Pokémon hurls itself off cliffs. As a result of its dives, its head has grown tough and as hard as tempered steel.

entries.name: Shelgon
entries.desc: Inside Shelgon’s armor-like shell, cells are in the midst of transformation to create an entirely new body. This Pokémon’s shell is extremely heavy, making its movements sluggish.

entries.name: Salamence
entries.desc: Salamence came about as a result of a strong, long-held dream of growing wings. It is said that this powerful desire triggered a sudden mutation in this Pokémon’s cells, causing it to sprout its magnificent wings.

entries.name: Beldum
entries.desc: Instead of blood, a powerful magnetic force courses throughout Beldum’s body. This Pokémon communicates with others by sending controlled pulses of magnetism.

entries.name: Metang
entries.desc: When two Beldum fuse together, Metang is formed. The brains of the Beldum are joined by a magnetic nervous system. By linking its brains magnetically, this Pokémon generates strong psychokinetic power.

entries.name: Metagross
entries.desc: Metagross has four brains in total. Combined, the four brains can breeze through difficult calculations faster than a supercomputer. This Pokémon can float in the air by tucking in its four legs.

entries.name: Regirock
entries.desc: Regirock was sealed away by people long ago. If this Pokémon’s body is damaged in battle, it is said to seek out suitable rocks on its own to repair itself.

entries.name: Regice
entries.desc: Regice’s body was made during an ice age. The deep-frozen body can’t be melted, even by fire. This Pokémon controls frigid air of -328 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Registeel
entries.desc: Registeel has a body that is harder than any kind of metal. Its body is apparently hollow. No one has any idea what this Pokémon eats.

entries.name: Latias
entries.desc: Latias is highly sensitive to the emotions of people. If it senses any hostility, this Pokémon ruffles the feathers all over its body and cries shrilly to intimidate the foe.

entries.name: Latios
entries.desc: Latios has the ability to make others see an image of what it has seen or imagines in its head. This Pokémon is intelligent and understands human speech.

entries.name: Kyogre
entries.desc: Through Primal Reversion and with nature’s full power, it will take back its true form. It can summon storms that cause the sea levels to rise.

entries.name: Groudon
entries.desc: Groudon is said to be the personification of the land itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Kyogre, as each sought to gain the power of nature.

entries.name: Rayquaza
entries.desc: Rayquaza is said to have lived for hundreds of millions of years. Legends remain of how it put to rest the clash between Kyogre and Groudon.

entries.name: Jirachi
entries.desc: A legend states that Jirachi will make true any wish that is written on notes attached to its head when it awakens. If this Pokémon senses danger, it will fight without awakening.

entries.name: Deoxys
entries.desc: The DNA of a space virus underwent a sudden mutation upon exposure to a laser beam and resulted in Deoxys. The crystalline organ on this Pokémon’s chest appears to be its brain.

entries.name: Turtwig
entries.desc: It undertakes photosynthesis with its body, making oxygen. The leaf on its head wilts if it is thirsty.

entries.name: Grotle
entries.desc: It knows where pure water wells up. It carries fellow Pokémon there on its back.

entries.name: Torterra
entries.desc: Small Pokémon occasionally gather on its unmoving back to begin building their nests.

entries.name: Chimchar
entries.desc: The gas made in its belly burns from its rear end. The fire burns weakly when it feels sick.

entries.name: Monferno
entries.desc: It uses ceilings and walls to launch aerial attacks. Its fiery tail is but one weapon.

entries.name: Infernape
entries.desc: It tosses its enemies around with agility. It uses all its limbs to fight in its own unique style.

entries.name: Piplup
entries.desc: Because it is very proud, it hates accepting food from people. Its thick down guards it from cold.

entries.name: Prinplup
entries.desc: It lives a solitary life. Its wings deliver wicked blows that can snap even the thickest of trees.

entries.name: Empoleon
entries.desc: The three horns that extend from its beak attest to its power. The leader has the biggest horns.

entries.name: Starly
entries.desc: They flock around mountains and fields, chasing after bug Pokémon. Their singing is noisy and annoying.

entries.name: Staravia
entries.desc: It lives in forests and fields. Squabbles over territory occur when flocks collide.

entries.name: Staraptor
entries.desc: When Staravia evolve into Staraptor, they leave the flock to live alone. They have sturdy wings.

entries.name: Bidoof
entries.desc: It constantly gnaws on logs and rocks to whittle down its front teeth. It nests alongside water.

entries.name: Bibarel
entries.desc: It makes its nest by damming streams with bark and mud. It is known as an industrious worker.

entries.name: Kricketot
entries.desc: When its antennae hit each other, it sounds like the music of a xylophone.

entries.name: Kricketune
entries.desc: It signals its emotions with its melodies. Scientists are studying these melodic patterns.

entries.name: Shinx
entries.desc: All of its fur dazzles if danger is sensed. It flees while the foe is momentarily blinded.

entries.name: Luxio
entries.desc: Strong electricity courses through the tips of its sharp claws. A light scratch causes fainting in foes.

entries.name: Luxray
entries.desc: Luxray’s ability to see through objects comes in handy when it’s scouting for danger.

entries.name: Budew
entries.desc: Over the winter, it closes its bud and endures the cold. In spring, the bud opens and releases pollen.

entries.name: Roserade
entries.desc: With the movements of a dancer, it strikes with whips that are densely lined with poison thorns.

entries.name: Cranidos
entries.desc: Its hard skull is its distinguishing feature. It snapped trees by headbutting them, and then it fed on their ripe berries.

entries.name: Rampardos
entries.desc: This ancient Pokémon used headbutts skillfully. Its brain was really small, so some theories suggest that its stupidity led to its extinction.

entries.name: Shieldon
entries.desc: Although its fossils can be found in layers of primeval rock, nothing but its face has ever been discovered.

entries.name: Bastiodon
entries.desc: This Pokémon is from roughly 100 million years ago. Its terrifyingly tough face is harder than steel.

entries.name: Burmy
entries.desc: If its cloak is broken in battle, it quickly remakes the cloak with materials nearby.

entries.name: Wormadam
entries.desc: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon’s body. The cloak is never shed.

entries.name: Mothim
entries.desc: It flutters around at night and steals honey from the Combee hive.

entries.name: Combee
entries.desc: It collects and delivers honey to its colony. At night, they cluster to form a beehive and sleep.

entries.name: Vespiquen
entries.desc: Its abdomen is a honeycomb for grubs. It raises its grubs on honey collected by Combee.

entries.name: Pachirisu
entries.desc: A pair may be seen rubbing their cheek pouches together in an effort to share stored electricity.

entries.name: Buizel
entries.desc: It inflates the flotation sac around its neck and pokes its head out of the water to see what is going on.

entries.name: Floatzel
entries.desc: Its flotation sac developed as a result of pursuing aquatic prey. It can double as a rubber raft.

entries.name: Cherubi
entries.desc: It evolves by sucking the energy out of the small ball where it had been storing nutrients.

entries.name: Cherrim
entries.desc: If it senses strong sunlight, it opens its folded petals to absorb the sun’s rays with its whole body.

entries.name: Cherrim

entries.name: Shellos
entries.desc: When it senses danger, a purple liquid oozes out of it. The liquid is thought to be something like greasy sweat.

entries.name: Shellos
entries.desc: When it senses danger, a purple liquid oozes out of it. The liquid is thought to be something like greasy sweat.

entries.name: Gastrodon
entries.desc: Their shape and color change, depending on their environment and diet. There are many of them at beaches where the waves are calm.

entries.name: Gastrodon
entries.desc: Their shape and color change, depending on their environment and diet. There are many of them at beaches where the waves are calm.

entries.name: Ambipom
entries.desc: It uses its tails for everything. If it wraps both of its tails around you and gives you a squeeze, that’s proof it really likes you.

entries.name: Drifloon
entries.desc: Wandering souls gathered together to form this Pokémon. When trying to make friends with children, Drifloon grabs them by the hand.

entries.name: Drifblim
entries.desc: The raw material for the gas inside its body is souls. When its body starts to deflate, it’s thought to carry away people and Pokémon.

entries.name: Buneary
entries.desc: The reason it keeps one ear rolled up is so it can launch a swift counterattack if it’s attacked by an enemy.

entries.name: Lopunny
entries.desc: It’s notably wary and has a dislike of fighting, but at the same time, it can deliver powerful kicks with its lithe legs.

entries.name: Mismagius
entries.desc: Its muttered curses can cause awful headaches or terrifying visions that torment others.

entries.name: Honchkrow
entries.desc: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.

entries.name: Glameow
entries.desc: When it’s happy, Glameow demonstrates beautiful movements of its tail, like a dancing ribbon.

entries.name: Purugly
entries.desc: To make itself appear intimidatingly beefy, it tightly cinches its waist with its twin tails.

entries.name: Chingling
entries.desc: There is an orb inside its mouth. When it hops, the orb bounces all over and makes a ringing sound.

entries.name: Stunky
entries.desc: It protects itself by spraying a noxious fluid from its rear. The stench lingers for 24 hours.

entries.name: Skuntank
entries.desc: It sprays a stinky fluid from its tail. The fluid smells worse the longer it is allowed to fester.

entries.name: Bronzor
entries.desc: Implements shaped like it were discovered in ancient tombs. It is unknown if they are related.

entries.name: Bronzong
entries.desc: Ancient people believed that petitioning Bronzong for rain was the way to make crops grow.

entries.name: Bonsly
entries.desc: If its body gets too damp, it will die. So, in a process reminiscent of sweating, its eyes expel moisture.

entries.name: Mime Jr.
entries.desc: When this gifted mimic surprises an opponent, Mime Jr. feels so happy that it ends up forgetting it was imitating something.

entries.name: Happiny
entries.desc: When it sees something round and white, Happiny puts it into the pouch on its stomach. It sometimes becomes overloaded and can’t move.

entries.name: Chatot
entries.desc: It can learn and speak human words. If they gather, they all learn the same saying.

entries.name: Spiritomb
entries.desc: It was bound to a fissure in an odd keystone as punishment for misdeeds 500 years ago.

entries.name: Gible
entries.desc: Its original home is an area much hotter than Alola. If you’re planning to live with one, your heating bill will soar.

entries.name: Gabite
entries.desc: It sheds its skin and gradually grows larger. Its scales can be ground into a powder and used as raw materials for traditional medicine.

entries.name: Garchomp
entries.desc: Its fine scales don’t just reduce wind resistance—their sharp edges also cause injury to any opponent who attacks it.

entries.name: Munchlax
entries.desc: Anything that looks edible, Munchlax will go on and swallow whole. Its stomach is tough enough to handle it even if the food has gone rotten.

entries.name: Riolu
entries.desc: It uses waves called auras to communicate with others of its kind. It doesn’t make any noise during this time, so its enemies can’t detect it.

entries.name: Lucario
entries.desc: Lucario reads its opponent’s feelings with its aura waves. It finds out things it would rather not know, so it gets stressed out easily.

entries.name: Hippopotas
entries.desc: It enshrouds itself with sand to protect itself from germs. It does not enjoy getting wet.

entries.name: Skorupi
entries.desc: It burrows under the sand to lie in wait for prey. Its tail claws can inject its prey with a savage poison.

entries.name: Drapion
entries.desc: It has the power in its clawed arms to make scrap of a car. The tips of its claws release poison.

entries.name: Croagunk
entries.desc: Inflating its poison sacs, it fills the area with an odd sound and hits flinching opponents with a poison jab.

entries.name: Toxicroak
entries.desc: Its knuckle claws secrete a toxin so vile that even a scratch could prove fatal.

entries.name: Carnivine
entries.desc: It binds itself to trees in marshes. It attracts prey with its sweet-smelling drool and gulps them down.

entries.name: Finneon
entries.desc: It lures in prey with its shining tail fins. It stays near the surface during the day and moves to the depths when night falls.

entries.name: Lumineon
entries.desc: They traverse the deep waters as if crawling over the seafloor. The fantastic lights of its fins shine like stars in the night sky.

entries.name: Mantyke
entries.desc: Mantyke are friendly toward people and will approach boats closely. The patterns on their backs differ depending on their habitat.

entries.name: Snover
entries.desc: In the spring, it grows berries with the texture of frozen treats around its belly.

entries.name: Abomasnow
entries.desc: It lives a quiet life on mountains that are perpetually covered in snow. It hides itself by whipping up blizzards.

entries.name: Weavile
entries.desc: Thanks to its increased intelligence, scrapping over food is a thing of the past. A scratch from its claws will give you a case of frostbite!

entries.name: Magnezone
entries.desc: There are still people who believe that this Pokémon came from outer space. It emanates a powerful magnetic field.

entries.name: Lickilicky
entries.desc: It uses its tongue much more skillfully than its hands or its feet. It can deftly pick up a single small bean with its tongue.

entries.name: Rhyperior
entries.desc: It puts rocks in holes in its palms and uses its muscles to shoot them. Geodude are shot at rare times.

entries.name: Tangrowth
entries.desc: Its vines grow so profusely that, in the warm season, you can’t even see its eyes.

entries.name: Electivire
entries.desc: A single Electivire can provide enough electricity for all the buildings in a big city for a year.

entries.name: Magmortar
entries.desc: Magmortar takes down its enemies by shooting fireballs, which burn them to a blackened crisp. It avoids this method when hunting prey.

entries.name: Togekiss
entries.desc: It shares many blessings with people who respect one another’s rights and avoid needless strife.

entries.name: Yanmega
entries.desc: This six-legged Pokémon is easily capable of transporting an adult in flight. The wings on its tail help it stay balanced.

entries.name: Leafeon
entries.desc: It gets its nutrition from photosynthesis. It lives a quiet life deep in forests where clean rivers flow.

entries.name: Glaceon
entries.desc: It can instantaneously freeze any moisture that’s around it, creating ice pellets to shoot at its prey.

entries.name: Gliscor
entries.desc: Its flight is soundless. It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey... Then its elongated fangs do the rest.

entries.name: Mamoswine
entries.desc: Its impressive tusks are made of ice. The population thinned when it turned warm after the ice age.

entries.name: Porygon-Z
entries.desc: A faulty update was added to its programming. Its behavior is noticeably strange, so the experiment may have been a failure.

entries.name: Gallade
entries.desc: A master of courtesy and swordsmanship, it fights using extending swords on its elbows.

entries.name: Probopass
entries.desc: It uses three small units to catch prey and battle enemies. The main body mostly just gives orders.

entries.name: Dusknoir
entries.desc: The antenna on its head captures radio waves from the world of spirits that command it to take people there.

entries.name: Froslass
entries.desc: It’s said that on nights of terrible blizzards, it comes down to human settlements. If you hear it knocking at your door, do not open it!

entries.desc: It sleeps at the bottom of a lake. Its spirit is said to leave its body to fly on the lake’s surface.

entries.name: Azelf
entries.desc: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf all came from the same egg.

entries.name: Dialga
entries.desc: It has the power to control time. It appears in Sinnoh-region myths as an ancient deity.

entries.name: Dialga
entries.desc: Radiant light caused Dialga to take on a form bearing a striking resemblance to the creator Pokémon. Dialga now wields such colossal strength that one must conclude this is its true form.

entries.name: Palkia
entries.desc: It has the ability to distort space. It is described as a deity in Sinnoh-region mythology.

entries.name: Palkia
entries.desc: It soars across the sky in a form that greatly resembles the creator of all things. Perhaps this imitation of appearance is Palkia’s strategy for gaining Arceus’s powers.

entries.name: Heatran
entries.desc: Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body. It makes its dwelling place in volcanic caves.

entries.name: Regigigas
entries.desc: There is an enduring legend that states this Pokémon towed continents with ropes.

entries.name: Giratina
entries.desc: It was banished for its violence. It silently gazed upon the old world from the Distortion World.

entries.desc: Those who sleep holding Cresselia’s feather are assured of joyful dreams. It is said to represent the crescent moon.

entries.name: Phione
entries.desc: It drifts in warm seas. It always returns to where it was born, no matter how far it may have drifted.

entries.name: Manaphy
entries.desc: It starts its life with a wondrous power that permits it to bond with any kind of Pokémon.

entries.name: Darkrai
entries.desc: It can lull people to sleep and make them dream. It is active during nights of the new moon.

entries.name: Shaymin
entries.desc: The blooming of Gracidea flowers confers the power of flight upon it. Feelings of gratitude are the message it delivers.

entries.desc: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being’s entire body will be overflowing with power.

entries.name: Snivy
entries.desc: They photosynthesize by bathing their tails in sunlight. When they are not feeling well, their tails droop.

entries.name: Servine
entries.desc: When it gets dirty, its leaves can’t be used in photosynthesis, so it always keeps itself clean.

entries.name: Serperior
entries.desc: It can stop its opponents’ movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.

entries.name: Tepig
entries.desc: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.

entries.name: Pignite
entries.desc: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.

entries.name: Emboar
entries.desc: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.

entries.name: Oshawott
entries.desc: It fights using the scalchop on its stomach. In response to an attack, it retaliates immediately by slashing.

entries.name: Dewott
entries.desc: As a result of strict training, each Dewott learns different forms for using the scalchops.

entries.name: Samurott
entries.desc: One swing of the sword incorporated in its armor can fell an opponent. A simple glare from one of them quiets everybody.

entries.name: Samurott
entries.desc: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon’s evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

entries.name: Patrat
entries.desc: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won’t notice a foe coming from behind.

entries.name: Watchog
entries.desc: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

entries.name: Lillipup
entries.desc: This Pokémon is popular with beginners because it’s intelligent, obedient to its Trainer’s commands, and easy to raise.

entries.name: Herdier
entries.desc: It has been living with people for so long that portrayals of it can be found on the walls of caves from long, long ago.

entries.name: Stoutland
entries.desc: Its fur is long and thick. A long time ago in cold regions, every household kept a Stoutland.

entries.name: Purrloin
entries.desc: They steal from people for fun, but their victims can’t help but forgive them. Their deceptively cute act is perfect.

entries.name: Liepard
entries.desc: Stealthily, it sneaks up on its target, striking from behind before its victim has a chance to react.

entries.name: Pansage
entries.desc: It’s good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It’s kind enough to share them with friends.

entries.name: Simisage
entries.desc: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

entries.name: Pansear
entries.desc: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Simisear
entries.desc: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.

entries.name: Panpour
entries.desc: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

entries.name: Simipour
entries.desc: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.

entries.name: Munna
entries.desc: It eats the dreams of people and Pokémon. When it eats a pleasant dream, it expels pink-colored mist.

entries.name: Musharna
entries.desc: The dream mist coming from its forehead changes into many different colors depending on the dream that was eaten.

entries.name: Pidove
entries.desc: These Pokémon live in cities. They are accustomed to people. Flocks often gather in parks and plazas.

entries.name: Tranquill
entries.desc: No matter where in the world it goes, it knows where its nest is, so it never gets separated from its Trainer.

entries.name: Unfezant
entries.desc: Males have plumage on their heads. They will never let themselves feel close to anyone other than their Trainers.

entries.name: Blitzle
entries.desc: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.

entries.name: Zebstrika
entries.desc: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.

entries.name: Roggenrola
entries.desc: It was found in a fissure in a layer of exposed rock. The material that makes up its body is dirt from several hundred years ago.

entries.name: Boldore
entries.desc: Its orange crystals are lumps of powerful energy. They’re valuable, so Boldore is sometimes targeted for them.

entries.name: Gigalith
entries.desc: It absorbs rays of sunlight and shoots out energy. It’s usually lurking deep beneath the surface.

entries.name: Woobat
entries.desc: The heart-shaped mark left on a body after a Woobat has been attached to it is said to bring good fortune.

entries.name: Swoobat
entries.desc: Anyone who comes into contact with the ultrasonic waves emitted by a courting male experiences a positive mood shift.

entries.name: Drilbur
entries.desc: By spinning its body, it can dig straight through the ground at a speed of 30 mph.

entries.name: Excadrill
entries.desc: More than 300 feet below the surface, they build mazelike nests. Their activity can be destructive to subway tunnels.

entries.name: Audino
entries.desc: It touches others with the feelers on its ears, using the sound of their heartbeats to tell how they are feeling.

entries.name: Timburr
entries.desc: Always carrying squared logs, they help out with construction. As they grow, they carry bigger logs.

entries.name: Gurdurr
entries.desc: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

entries.name: Conkeldurr
entries.desc: Rather than rely on force, they master moves that utilize the centrifugal force of spinning concrete.

entries.name: Tympole
entries.desc: By vibrating its cheeks, it emits sound waves imperceptible to humans. It uses the rhythm of these sounds to talk.

entries.name: Palpitoad
entries.desc: It lives in the water and on land. It uses its long, sticky tongue to immobilize its opponents.

entries.name: Seismitoad
entries.desc: They shoot paralyzing liquid from their head bumps. They use vibration to hurt their opponents.

entries.name: Throh
entries.desc: When it encounters a foe bigger than itself, it wants to throw it. It changes belts as it gets stronger.

entries.name: Sawk
entries.desc: Tying their belts gets them pumped and makes their punches more destructive. Disturbing their training angers them.

entries.name: Sewaddle
entries.desc: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.

entries.name: Swadloon
entries.desc: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

entries.name: Leavanny
entries.desc: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

entries.name: Venipede
entries.desc: Its bite injects a potent poison, enough to paralyze large bird Pokémon that try to prey on it.

entries.name: Whirlipede
entries.desc: It is usually motionless, but when attacked, it rotates at high speed and then crashes into its opponent.

entries.name: Scolipede
entries.desc: With quick movements, it chases down its foes, attacking relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.

entries.name: Cottonee
entries.desc: When attacked, it expels cotton from its body to create a diversion. The cotton it loses grows back in quickly.

entries.name: Whimsicott
entries.desc: Whimsicott doesn’t live in a fixed location. It floats around on whirling winds, appearing all over the place to perform its mischief.

entries.name: Petilil
entries.desc: They prefer clean water and soil. When the environment they live in turns bad, the whole bunch will up and move to a new area.

entries.name: Lilligant
entries.desc: It’s well liked by other Pokémon because of its beauty. The flower on its head needs constant care, or it will soon wither and rot.

entries.name: Lilligant
entries.desc: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

entries.name: Basculin
entries.desc: When a school of Basculin appears in a lake, everything else disappears, except for Corphish and Crawdaunt. That’s how violent Basculin are.

entries.name: Krokorok
entries.desc: It buries some of its prey in the sand to use as emergency meals when its hunts are unsuccessful.

entries.name: Krookodile
entries.desc: It conceals itself in sandstorms that Flygon whip up and waits patiently for prey to appear.

entries.name: Darumaka
entries.desc: When it sleeps, it pulls its limbs into its body and its internal fire goes down to 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Darumaka
entries.desc: It lived in snowy areas for so long that its fire sac cooled off and atrophied. It now has an organ that generates cold instead.

entries.name: Darmanitan
entries.desc: Its internal fire burns at 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.

entries.name: Darmanitan
entries.desc: On days when blizzards blow through, it comes down to where people live. It stashes food in the snowball on its head, taking it home for later.

entries.name: Maractus
entries.desc: Arid regions are their habitat. They move rhythmically, making a sound similar to maracas.

entries.name: Dwebble
entries.desc: When it finds a stone of a suitable size, it secretes a liquid from its mouth to open up a hole to crawl into.

entries.name: Crustle
entries.desc: Competing for territory, Crustle fight viciously. The one whose boulder is broken is the loser of the battle.

entries.name: Scraggy
entries.desc: It stretches its saggy skin up to its neck to protect itself. The saggier their skin, the more respect they garner.

entries.name: Scrafty
entries.desc: It taunts its opponents by spitting. It has a certain territory that it never leaves its whole life long.

entries.name: Sigilyph
entries.desc: The guardians of an ancient city, they always fly the same route while keeping watch for invaders.

entries.name: Yamask
entries.desc: Each of them carries a mask that used to be its face when it was human. Sometimes they look at it and cry.

entries.name: Yamask
entries.desc: A clay slab with cursed engravings took possession of a Yamask. The slab is said to be absorbing the Yamask’s dark power.

entries.name: Cofagrigus
entries.desc: Grave robbers who mistake them for real coffins and get too close end up trapped inside their bodies.

entries.name: Tirtouga
entries.desc: Its hunting grounds encompassed a broad area, from the land to more than half a mile deep in the ocean.

entries.name: Carracosta
entries.desc: Carracosta eats every last bit of the prey it catches, even the shells and bones, to further strengthen its sturdy shell.

entries.name: Archen
entries.desc: Restored from a fossil, this ancient bird Pokémon has wings but can’t yet fly.

entries.name: Archeops
entries.desc: Said to be an ancestor of bird Pokémon, the muscles it uses to flap its wings are still weak, so it needs a long runway in order to take off.

entries.name: Trubbish
entries.desc: If a young Pokémon or child breathes in the toxic gas that Trubbish belches out, it could be a life-threatening situation.

entries.name: Garbodor
entries.desc: Some say the reason Garbodor in Alola are a little stronger than their counterparts elsewhere is the presence of Muk, their natural enemy.

entries.name: Zorua
entries.desc: If a normally talkative child suddenly stops talking, it may have been replaced by Zorua.

entries.name: Zorua
entries.desc: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

entries.name: Zoroark
entries.desc: If it thinks humans are going to discover its den, Zoroark shows them visions that make them wander around in the woods.

entries.name: Zoroark
entries.desc: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark’s own body.

entries.name: Minccino
entries.desc: When its tail has gotten dirty from self-cleaning or from cleaning its nest, Minccino spends a whole day washing its tail in clean spring water.

entries.name: Cinccino
entries.desc: The oil that seeps from its body is really smooth. For people troubled by bad skin, this oil is an effective treatment.

entries.name: Gothita
entries.desc: They intently observe both Trainers and Pokémon. Apparently, they are looking at something that only Gothita can see.

entries.name: Gothorita
entries.desc: According to many old tales, it creates friends for itself by controlling sleeping children on starry nights.

entries.name: Gothitelle
entries.desc: They can predict the future from the placement and movement of the stars. They can see Trainers’ life spans.

entries.name: Solosis
entries.desc: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.

entries.name: Duosion
entries.desc: When their two divided brains think the same thoughts, their psychic power is maximized.

entries.name: Reuniclus
entries.desc: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.

entries.name: Ducklett
entries.desc: They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.

entries.name: Swanna
entries.desc: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.

entries.name: Vanillite
entries.desc: When the morning sun hit an icicle, it wished not to melt, and thus Vanillite was born. At night, it buries itself in snow to sleep.

entries.name: Vanillish
entries.desc: This hearty Pokémon survived the Ice Age. It’s incredibly popular in very hot regions.

entries.name: Vanilluxe
entries.desc: Vanilluxe is born when two Vanillish, half-melted by the day’s light, stick to each other and freeze together in the cold return of night.

entries.name: Klinklang

entries.name: Tynamo
entries.desc: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.

entries.name: Eelektrik
entries.desc: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

entries.name: Eelektross
entries.desc: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

entries.desc: This Pokémon is shrouded in mystery. It’s said to have appeared from a UFO that fell from the sky about 50 years ago.

entries.name: Beheeyem
entries.desc: It has strong psychic powers. Using its fingers that flash three different colors, it controls its opponents and rewrites their memories.

entries.name: Litwick
entries.desc: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.

entries.name: Lampent
entries.desc: It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.

entries.name: Chandelure
entries.desc: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.

entries.name: Axew
entries.desc: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.

entries.name: Fraxure
entries.desc: A broken tusk will not grow back, so it diligently sharpens its tusks on river rocks after the end of a battle.

entries.name: Haxorus
entries.desc: Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.

entries.name: Cubchoo
entries.desc: Their snot is a barometer of health. When healthy, their snot is sticky and the power of their ice moves increases.

entries.name: Beartic
entries.desc: It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.

entries.name: Cryogonal
entries.desc: They are composed of ice crystals. They capture prey with chains of ice, freezing the prey at -148 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Shelmet
entries.desc: It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.

entries.name: Accelgor
entries.desc: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.

entries.name: Stunfisk
entries.desc: It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.

entries.name: Stunfisk
entries.desc: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.

entries.name: Mienfoo
entries.desc: They seclude themselves in the mountains and devote themselves to training. The form of their kicks and chops differs from pack to pack.

entries.name: Mienshao
entries.desc: When Mienshao lets out a bizarre wail, you’re in danger. A flurry of kicks and chops too fast to see is about to be unleashed!

entries.name: Druddigon
entries.desc: It infiltrates tunnels that Pokémon like Diglett and Dugtrio have dug and quietly waits for prey to pass through.

entries.name: Golett
entries.desc: Although ancient people apparently built it by working with clay, the source of its energy is unclear.

entries.name: Golurk
entries.desc: When the seal on its chest is removed, it rages indiscriminately, turning the whole town around it into a mountain of rubble.

entries.name: Pawniard
entries.desc: It follows Bisharp’s orders to a tee when it attacks enemies. After slashing an opponent, Pawniard clangs both of its blades together.

entries.name: Bisharp
entries.desc: It leads a group of Pawniard. Bisharp doesn’t even change its expression when it deals the finishing blow to an opponent.

entries.name: Braviary

entries.name: Braviary

entries.name: Vullaby

entries.name: Mandibuzz
entries.desc: It’s always searching for food for Vullaby. When it finds a weak Pokémon, Mandibuzz swoops it right off to its nest.

entries.name: Heatmor

entries.name: Durant
entries.desc: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.

entries.name: Deino
entries.desc: Lacking sight, it’s unaware of its surroundings, so it bumps into things and eats anything that moves.

entries.name: Zweilous
entries.desc: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.

entries.name: Hydreigon
entries.desc: It responds to movement by attacking. This scary, three-headed Pokémon devours everything in its path!

entries.name: Larvesta
entries.desc: It protects itself with flame. Long years ago, people believed Larvesta had a nest on the sun.

entries.name: Volcarona
entries.desc: According to legends, it was hatched from a flaming cocoon to save people and Pokémon that were suffering from the cold.

entries.name: Cobalion
entries.desc: It has a body and heart of steel. It worked with its allies to punish people when they hurt Pokémon.

entries.name: Terrakion
entries.desc: Spoken of in legend, this Pokémon used its phenomenal power to destroy a castle in its effort to protect Pokémon.

entries.name: Virizion
entries.desc: Legends say this Pokémon confounded opponents with its swift movements.

entries.desc: With their powerful ears, they can heft boulders of a ton or more with ease. They can be a big help at construction sites.

entries.name: Espurr
entries.desc: The organ that emits its intense psychic power is sheltered by its ears to keep power from leaking out.

entries.name: Meowstic
entries.desc: When in danger, it raises its ears and releases enough psychic power to grind a 10-ton truck into dust.

entries.name: Honedge
entries.desc: Apparently this Pokémon is born when a departed spirit inhabits a sword. It attaches itself to people and drinks their life force.

entries.name: Doublade
entries.desc: When Honedge evolves, it divides into two swords, which cooperate via telepathy to coordinate attacks and slash their enemies to ribbons.

entries.name: Aegislash
entries.desc: Generations of kings were attended by these Pokémon, which used their spectral power to manipulate and control people and Pokémon.

entries.name: Spritzee
entries.desc: It emits a scent that enraptures those who smell it. This fragrance changes depending on what it has eaten.

entries.name: Aromatisse
entries.desc: It devises various scents, pleasant and unpleasant, and emits scents that its enemies dislike in order to gain an edge in battle.

entries.name: Swirlix
entries.desc: To entangle its opponents in battle, it extrudes white threads as sweet and sticky as cotton candy.

entries.name: Slurpuff
entries.desc: It can distinguish the faintest of scents. It puts its sensitive sense of smell to use by helping pastry chefs in their work.

entries.name: Inkay
entries.desc: Opponents who stare at the flashing of the light-emitting spots on its body become dazed and lose their will to fight.

entries.name: Malamar
entries.desc: It wields the most compelling hypnotic powers of any Pokémon, and it forces others to do whatever it wants.

entries.name: Binacle
entries.desc: Two Binacle live together on one rock. When they fight, one of them will move to a different rock.

entries.name: Barbaracle
entries.desc: When they evolve, two Binacle multiply into seven. They fight with the power of seven Binacle.

entries.name: Skrelp
entries.desc: Camouflaged as rotten kelp, they spray liquid poison on prey that approaches unawares and then finish it off.

entries.name: Dragalge
entries.desc: Their poison is strong enough to eat through the hull of a tanker, and they spit it indiscriminately at anything that enters their territory.

entries.name: Clauncher
entries.desc: They knock down flying prey by firing compressed water from their massive claws like shooting a pistol.

entries.name: Clawitzer
entries.desc: Their enormous claws launch cannonballs of water powerful enough to pierce tanker hulls.

entries.name: Helioptile
entries.desc: They make their home in deserts. They can generate their energy from basking in the sun, so eating food is not a requirement.

entries.name: Heliolisk
entries.desc: They flare their frills and generate energy. A single Heliolisk can generate sufficient electricity to power a skyscraper.

entries.name: Tyrunt
entries.desc: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. If something happens that it doesn’t like, it throws a tantrum and runs wild.

entries.name: Tyrantrum
entries.desc: Thanks to its gargantuan jaws, which could shred thick metal plates as if they were paper, it was invincible in the ancient world it once inhabited.

entries.name: Amaura
entries.desc: This ancient Pokémon was restored from part of its body that had been frozen in ice for over 100 million years.

entries.name: Aurorus
entries.desc: The diamond-shaped crystals on its body expel air as cold as -240 degrees Fahrenheit, surrounding its enemies and encasing them in ice.

entries.name: Sylveon
entries.desc: It sends a soothing aura from its ribbonlike feelers to calm fights.

entries.name: Hawlucha
entries.desc: Although its body is small, its proficient fighting skills enable it to keep up with big bruisers like Machamp and Hariyama.

entries.name: Dedenne
entries.desc: Its whiskers serve as antennas. By sending and receiving electrical waves, it can communicate with others over vast distances.

entries.name: Carbink
entries.desc: Born from the temperatures and pressures deep underground, it fires beams from the stone in its head.

entries.name: Goomy
entries.desc: The weakest Dragon-type Pokémon, it lives in damp, shady places, so its body doesn’t dry out.

entries.name: Sliggoo
entries.desc: It drives away opponents by excreting a sticky liquid that can dissolve anything. Its eyes devolved, so it can’t see anything.

entries.name: Sliggoo
entries.desc: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui’s water.

entries.name: Goodra
entries.desc: This very friendly Dragon-type Pokémon will hug its beloved Trainer, leaving that Trainer covered in sticky slime.

entries.name: Goodra
entries.desc: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.

entries.name: Klefki
entries.desc: These key collectors threaten any attackers by fiercely jingling their keys at them.

entries.name: Phantump
entries.desc: These Pokémon are created when spirits possess rotten tree stumps. They prefer to live in abandoned forests.

entries.name: Trevenant
entries.desc: It can control trees at will. It will trap people who harm the forest, so they can never leave.

entries.name: Pumpkaboo
entries.desc: The pumpkin body is inhabited by a spirit trapped in this world. As the sun sets, it becomes restless and active.

entries.name: Gourgeist
entries.desc: Singing in eerie voices, they wander town streets on the night of the new moon. Anyone who hears their song is cursed.

entries.name: Bergmite
entries.desc: It blocks opponents’ attacks with the ice that shields its body. It uses cold air to repair any cracks with new ice.

entries.name: Avalugg
entries.desc: Its ice-covered body is as hard as steel. Its cumbersome frame crushes anything that stands in its way.

entries.name: Avalugg
entries.desc: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

entries.name: Noibat
entries.desc: They live in pitch-black caves. Their enormous ears can emit ultrasonic waves of 200,000 hertz.

entries.name: Noivern
entries.desc: They fly around on moonless nights and attack careless prey. Nothing can beat them in a battle in the dark.

entries.name: Xerneas
entries.desc: Legends say it can share eternal life. It slept for a thousand years in the form of a tree before its revival.

entries.name: Yveltal
entries.desc: When this legendary Pokémon’s wings and tail feathers spread wide and glow red, it absorbs the life force of living creatures.

entries.name: Zygarde
entries.desc: When the Kalos region’s ecosystem falls into disarray, it appears and reveals its secret power.

entries.name: Zygarde
entries.desc: When the Kalos region’s ecosystem falls into disarray, it appears and reveals its secret power.

entries.name: Diancie
entries.desc: A sudden transformation of Carbink, its pink, glimmering body is said to be the loveliest sight in the whole world.

entries.name: Hoopa
entries.desc: In its true form, it possess a huge amount of power. Legends of its avarice tell how it once carried off an entire castle to gain the treasure hidden within.

entries.name: Hoopa
entries.desc: It is said to be able to seize anything it desires with its six rings and six huge arms. With its power sealed, it is transformed into a much smaller form.

entries.name: Volcanion
entries.desc: It lets out billows of steam and disappears into the dense fog. It’s said to live in mountains where humans do not tread.

entries.name: Rowlet
entries.desc: It feels relaxed in tight, dark places and has been known to use its Trainer’s pocket or bag as a nest.

entries.name: Dartrix
entries.desc: Supremely sensitive to the presence of others, it can detect opponents standing behind it, flinging its sharp feathers to take them out.

entries.name: Decidueye
entries.desc: Decidueye can nock and fire an arrow at an enemy in a tenth of a second, so its battles are decided in the blink of an eye.

entries.name: Decidueye
entries.desc: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye’s feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui’s extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

entries.name: Litten
entries.desc: Its coat regrows twice a year. When the time comes, Litten sets its own body on fire and burns away the old fur.

entries.name: Torracat
entries.desc: When its mane is standing on end, you can tell it’s feeling good. When it isn’t feeling well, its fur will lie down flat.

entries.name: Incineroar
entries.desc: When its fighting spirit is set alight, the flames around its waist become especially intense.

entries.name: Popplio
entries.desc: Popplio gets on top of its bouncy water balloons to jump higher. It’s quite the acrobatic fighter!

entries.name: Brionne
entries.desc: It attacks by smacking its enemies with the exploding water balloons that it creates.

entries.name: Primarina
entries.desc: Also known as a songstress, it has a fantastical look on moonlit nights when it leads its colony in song.

entries.name: Pikipek
entries.desc: It may look spindly, but its neck muscles are heavy-duty. It can peck at a tree 16 times per second!

entries.name: Trumbeak
entries.desc: From its mouth, it fires the seeds of berries it has eaten. The scattered seeds give rise to new plants.

entries.name: Toucannon
entries.desc: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.

entries.name: Yungoos
entries.desc: Although it will eat anything, it prefers fresh living things, so it marches down streets in search of prey.

entries.name: Gumshoos
entries.desc: Patient by nature, this Pokémon loses control of itself and pounces when it spots its favorite meal—Rattata!

entries.name: Grubbin
entries.desc: It spits a sticky thread to stop opponents in their tracks, and then it grabs them in its sharp, sturdy mandibles to take them down.

entries.name: Charjabug
entries.desc: Its stout shell provides excellent defense from attacks. It uses electricity on persistent opponents.

entries.name: Vikavolt
entries.desc: Vikavolt flusters opponents with acrobatic flying maneuvers. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electric beam attack.

entries.name: Crabrawler
entries.desc: Crabrawler has been known to mistake Exeggutor for a coconut tree and climb it. The enraged Exeggutor shakes it off and stomps it.

entries.name: Crabominable
entries.desc: Before it stops to think, it just starts pummeling. There are records of its turning back avalanches with a flurry of punches.

entries.name: Oricorio
entries.desc: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.

entries.name: Oricorio
entries.desc: This Oricorio has drunk bright yellow nectar. When it sees someone looking glum, it will try to cheer them up with a dance.

entries.name: Oricorio
entries.desc: This Oricorio has sipped pink nectar. It gets so caught up in its dancing that it sometimes doesn’t hear its Trainer’s orders.

entries.name: Oricorio
entries.desc: This Oricorio has sipped purple nectar. Some dancers use its graceful, elegant dancing as inspiration.

entries.name: Cutiefly
entries.desc: Cutiefly can pick up the auras of living things. It skillfully reads those auras to predict its foes’ movements and make fools of them.

entries.name: Ribombee
entries.desc: It can predict the weather from moisture levels and wind direction. Ribombee only reveals itself when there are a few clear days in a row.

entries.name: Rockruff
entries.desc: When it rubs the rocks on its neck against you, that’s proof of its love for you. However, the rocks are sharp, so the gesture is quite painful!

entries.name: Lycanroc
entries.desc: The rocks in its mane are sharper than a knife. Fragments that break off are treasured as good luck charms.

entries.name: Lycanroc
entries.desc: It has no problem ignoring orders it doesn’t like. It doesn’t seem to mind getting hurt at all—as long as it can finish off its opponent.

entries.name: Lycanroc
entries.desc: This strange form is the result of its evolving at dusk. It’s very rare in Alola.

entries.name: Wishiwashi
entries.desc: When it’s in a jam, its shining eyes attract others of its kind. The light from its eyes is visible almost 25 miles away.

entries.name: Mareanie
entries.desc: Aside from its head, its body parts regenerate quickly if they’re cut off. After a good night’s sleep, Mareanie is back to normal.

entries.name: Toxapex
entries.desc: With its 12 legs, it creates a dome to shelter within. The flow of the tides doesn’t affect Toxapex in there, so it’s very comfortable.

entries.name: Mudbray
entries.desc: Possessing mighty power, Mudbray can be loaded with 50 times its own body weight and will be totally fine.

entries.name: Mudsdale
entries.desc: It can trudge mountain roads without rest for three days and three nights, all the while dragging a 10-ton load.

entries.name: Dewpider
entries.desc: It can only breathe oxygen that has dissolved in water, so it wears a water bubble on its head when it walks around on land.

entries.name: Araquanid
entries.desc: It has a habit of storing things it values in its water bubble. If its Trainer doesn’t watch out, Araquanid will try to put them in its bubble!

entries.name: Fomantis
entries.desc: It loves the sunshine. When it basks in the sunlight regularly, it grows up with vivid coloration.

entries.name: Lurantis
entries.desc: As it slashes into its enemies, it looks like it’s dancing. Its elegant appearance has led some to call it the most glamorous Grass Pokémon.

entries.name: Morelull
entries.desc: It likes damp dark places. When night falls, the spores filling the caps of its mushrooms glow.

entries.name: Shiinotic
entries.desc: When it starts fighting for territory with Parasect, the entire area gets completely coated in spores!

entries.name: Salandit
entries.desc: It weakens opponents and sends them reeling with its poisonous gas. Salandit doesn’t deal well with Spinda, since it’s always reeling.

entries.name: Salazzle
entries.desc: It punishes Salandit that couldn’t bring it food with a fierce slap of its flame-spewing palm.

entries.name: Stufful
entries.desc: Stufful hates to be hugged or touched in any way. It will squirm, thrash, and resist with amazing power.

entries.name: Bewear
entries.desc: It boasts tremendous physical strength. Many people call it the most dangerous Pokémon in the Alola region.

entries.name: Bounsweet
entries.desc: It tries to resist being swallowed by a bird Pokémon by spinning the sepals on its head. It’s usually a fruitless attempt.

entries.name: Steenee
entries.desc: It bounces around, swinging the sepals on its head with abandon. They’re quite painful when they smack you!

entries.name: Tsareena
entries.desc: A Pokémon with an aggressive personality and a mastery of kicking, it cackles every time it kicks an opponent.

entries.name: Comfey
entries.desc: It picks flowers and sticks them to its body with fluids it produces. The aroma that wafts from its petals has a healing effect.

entries.name: Oranguru
entries.desc: Oranguru don’t get along with each other, so they’re always engaging in battles of wits to decide which one is superior.

entries.name: Passimian
entries.desc: Berries are its weapons as well as the staple of its diet. The one that can throw a berry the farthest is the boss of the troop.

entries.name: Wimpod
entries.desc: An astonishingly cowardly Pokémon, Wimpod will whir its legs at high speeds to run away if anything comes near it.

entries.name: Golisopod
entries.desc: Its claws, which it can extend and retract at will, are its greatest weapons. Golisopod is sometimes accompanied by Wimpod.

entries.name: Sandygast
entries.desc: If you build sand mounds when you’re playing, destroy them before you go home, or they may get possessed and become Sandygast.

entries.name: Palossand
entries.desc: Once it has whipped up a sandstorm to halt its opponents in their tracks, this terrifying Pokémon snatches away their vitality.

entries.name: Pyukumuku
entries.desc: Its entire body is covered in its own slime. If you accidentally step on one, you’ll slip, and it will get mad and smack you!

entries.name: Type: Null
entries.desc: There’s danger of its going on a rampage, so its true power is sealed away beneath its control mask.

entries.name: Silvally
entries.desc: Through the bond it formed with its Trainer, its will was strengthened, and it was able to destroy its control mask.

entries.name: Minior
entries.desc: Although its outer shell is uncommonly durable, the shock of falling to the ground smashes the shell to smithereens.
