entries.name: Komala
entries.desc: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.

entries.name: Turtonator
entries.desc: Its exploding shell poses a real danger but is sensitive to moisture. On rainy days, Turtonator takes silent refuge in caves.

entries.name: Togedemaru
entries.desc: Its capacity to produce electricity is somewhat limited, so it gets charged up by letting lightning strike it!

entries.name: Mimikyu
entries.desc: A gust of wind revealed what hides under this Pokémon’s rag to a passing Trainer, who went home and died painfully that very night.

entries.name: Bruxish
entries.desc: Its skin is thick enough to fend off Mareanie’s spikes. With its robust teeth, Bruxish crunches up the spikes and eats them.

entries.name: Drampa
entries.desc: It appears in towns and plays with the children. Drampa will protect kids when they’re in danger, so their moms don’t have to worry.

entries.name: Dhelmise
entries.desc: Its chain-like green seaweed can stretch outward for hundreds of yards. For some reason, it gets along well with Skrelp.

entries.name: Jangmo-o
entries.desc: It will never show an enemy its back in battle. Ancient warriors liked Jangmo-o for its valiant disposition and made it one of their own.

entries.name: Hakamo-o
entries.desc: The scales it sheds can be molded and processed to make pots and pans. They conduct heat well, so they’re a popular item.

entries.name: Kommo-o
entries.desc: It battles valiantly with its fists, which are armored in steel scales. Kommo-o specializes in uppercuts.

entries.name: Tapu Koko
entries.desc: The lightning-wielding guardian deity of Melemele, Tapu Koko is brimming with curiosity and appears before people from time to time.

entries.name: Tapu Lele
entries.desc: Although called a guardian deity, Tapu Lele is devoid of guilt about its cruel disposition and can be described as nature incarnate.

entries.name: Tapu Bulu
entries.desc: It makes ringing sounds with its tail to let others know where it is, avoiding unneeded conflicts. This guardian deity of Ula’ula controls plants.

entries.name: Tapu Fini
entries.desc: Although it’s called a guardian deity, terrible calamities sometimes befall those who recklessly approach Tapu Fini.

entries.name: Cosmog
entries.desc: Whether or not it’s a Pokémon from this world is a mystery. When it’s in a jam, it warps away to a safe place to hide.

entries.name: Cosmoem
entries.desc: As it absorbs light, Cosmoem continues to grow. Its golden shell is surprisingly solid.

entries.name: Solgaleo
entries.desc: In writings from the distant past, it’s called by the name “the beast that devours the sun."

entries.name: Lunala
entries.desc: It sometimes summons unknown powers and life-forms here to this world from holes that lead to other worlds.

entries.name: Nihilego
entries.desc: It appeared in this world from an Ultra Wormhole. Nihilego appears to be a parasite that lives by feeding on people and Pokémon.

entries.name: Buzzwole
entries.desc: Buzzwole goes around showing off its abnormally swollen muscles. It is one kind of Ultra Beast.

entries.name: Pheromosa
entries.desc: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.

entries.name: Xurkitree
entries.desc: They’ve been dubbed Ultra Beasts. Some of them stand unmoving, like trees, with their arms and legs stuck into the ground.

entries.name: Celesteela
entries.desc: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.

entries.name: Kartana
entries.desc: This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.

entries.name: Guzzlord
entries.desc: An unknown life-form called a UB. It may be constantly hungry—it is certainly always devouring something.

entries.name: Necrozma
entries.desc: Light is the source of its energy. If it isn’t devouring light, impurities build up in it and on it, and Necrozma darkens and stops moving.

entries.name: Necrozma
entries.desc: This is its form while it is devouring the light of Solgaleo. It pounces on foes and then slashes them with the claws on its four limbs and back.

entries.name: Necrozma
entries.desc: This is its form while it’s devouring the light of Lunala. It grasps foes in its giant claws and rips them apart with brute force.

entries.name: Magearna
entries.desc: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.

entries.name: Marshadow
entries.desc: It sinks into the shadows of people and Pokémon, where it can understand their feelings and copy their capabilities.

entries.name: Poipole
entries.desc: An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.

entries.name: Naganadel
entries.desc: One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.

entries.name: Stakataka
entries.desc: When stone walls started moving and attacking, the brute’s true identity was this mysterious life-form, which brings to mind an Ultra Beast.

entries.name: Blacephalon
entries.desc: A UB that appeared from an Ultra Wormhole, it causes explosions, then takes advantage of opponents’ surprise to rob them of their vitality.

entries.name: Zeraora
entries.desc: It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.

entries.name: Meltan
entries.desc: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.

entries.name: Melmetal
entries.desc: Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.

entries.name: Grookey
entries.desc: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

entries.name: Thwackey
entries.desc: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

entries.name: Rillaboom
entries.desc: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

entries.name: Scorbunny
entries.desc: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon’s body. Once that happens, it’s ready to fight at full power.

entries.name: Raboot
entries.desc: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.

entries.name: Cinderace
entries.desc: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.

entries.name: Sobble
entries.desc: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won’t be able to resist weeping.

entries.name: Drizzile
entries.desc: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.

entries.name: Inteleon
entries.desc: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.

entries.name: Skwovet
entries.desc: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.

entries.name: Greedent
entries.desc: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn’t notice the loss.

entries.name: Rookidee
entries.desc: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.

entries.name: Corvisquire
entries.desc: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.

entries.name: Corviknight
entries.desc: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.

entries.name: Blipbug
entries.desc: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t.

entries.name: Dottler
entries.desc: It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.

entries.name: Orbeetle
entries.desc: It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.

entries.name: Nickit
entries.desc: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

entries.name: Thievul
entries.desc: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

entries.name: Gossifleur
entries.desc: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.

entries.name: Eldegoss
entries.desc: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.

entries.name: Wooloo
entries.desc: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.

entries.name: Dubwool
entries.desc: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.

entries.name: Chewtle
entries.desc: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.

entries.name: Drednaw
entries.desc: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.

entries.name: Yamper
entries.desc: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

entries.name: Boltund
entries.desc: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

entries.name: Rolycoly
entries.desc: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.

entries.name: Carkol
entries.desc: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.

entries.name: Coalossal
entries.desc: It’s usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Applin
entries.desc: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more.

entries.name: Flapple
entries.desc: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.

entries.name: Appletun
entries.desc: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.

entries.name: Silicobra
entries.desc: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.

entries.name: Sandaconda
entries.desc: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.

entries.name: Cramorant
entries.desc: It’s so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it’s battling midfight.

entries.name: Arrokuda
entries.desc: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It’s very proud of that jaw.

entries.name: Barraskewda
entries.desc: This Pokémon has a jaw that’s as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda’s flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.

entries.name: Toxel
entries.desc: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.

entries.name: Toxtricity
entries.desc: Capable of generating 15,000 volts of electricity, this Pokémon looks down on all that would challenge it.

entries.name: Toxtricity
entries.desc: When this Pokémon sounds as if it’s strumming a guitar, it’s actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.

entries.name: Sizzlipede
entries.desc: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

entries.name: Centiskorch
entries.desc: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

entries.name: Clobbopus
entries.desc: It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

entries.name: Grapploct
entries.desc: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.

entries.name: Sinistea
entries.desc: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.

entries.name: Sinistea
entries.desc: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.

entries.name: Polteageist
entries.desc: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.

entries.name: Polteageist
entries.desc: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.

entries.name: Hatenna
entries.desc: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.

entries.name: Hattrem
entries.desc: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.

entries.name: Hatterene
entries.desc: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.

entries.name: Impidimp
entries.desc: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.

entries.name: Morgrem
entries.desc: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.

entries.name: Grimmsnarl
entries.desc: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.

entries.name: Obstagoon
entries.desc: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.

entries.name: Perrserker
entries.desc: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.

entries.name: Cursola
entries.desc: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit.

entries.name: Sirfetch'd
entries.desc: Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat.

entries.name: Mr. Rime
entries.desc: It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.

entries.name: Runerigus
entries.desc: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.

entries.name: Milcery
entries.desc: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.

entries.name: Alcremie
entries.desc: When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it’s decorated with cream.

entries.name: Falinks
entries.desc: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass’s orders are absolute.

entries.name: Pincurchin
entries.desc: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.

entries.name: Snom
entries.desc: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.

entries.name: Frosmoth
entries.desc: Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.name: Stonjourner
entries.desc: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

entries.name: Eiscue
entries.desc: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.

entries.name: Indeedee
entries.desc: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.

entries.name: Indeedee
entries.desc: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.

entries.name: Morpeko
entries.desc: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity.

entries.name: Cufant
entries.desc: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.

entries.name: Copperajah
entries.desc: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.

entries.name: Dracozolt
entries.desc: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.

entries.name: Arctozolt
entries.desc: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.

entries.name: Dracovish
entries.desc: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.

entries.name: Arctovish
entries.desc: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.

entries.name: Duraludon
entries.desc: Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.

entries.name: Dreepy
entries.desc: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.

entries.name: Drakloak
entries.desc: It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.

entries.name: Dragapult
entries.desc: When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.

entries.name: Zacian
entries.desc: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.

entries.name: Zamazenta
entries.desc: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.

entries.name: Eternatus
entries.desc: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.

entries.name: Kubfu
entries.desc: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.

entries.name: Urshifu
entries.desc: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.

entries.name: Urshifu
entries.desc: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.

entries.name: Zarude
entries.desc: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.

entries.name: Regieleki
entries.desc: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.

entries.name: Regidrago
entries.desc: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.

entries.name: Glastrier
entries.desc: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.

entries.name: Spectrier
entries.desc: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.

entries.name: Calyrex
entries.desc: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.

entries.name: Wyrdeer
entries.desc: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

entries.name: Kleavor
entries.desc: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one’s only recourse is to flee.

entries.name: Ursaluna
entries.desc: I believe it was Hisui’s swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

entries.name: Basculegion
entries.desc: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui’s rivers is Basculegion’s equal.

entries.name: Sneasler
entries.desc: Because of Sneasler’s virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

entries.name: Overqwil
entries.desc: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname “sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

entries.name: Enamorus
entries.desc: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon’s love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

entries.name: Enamorus
entries.desc: A different guise from its feminine humanoid form. From the clouds, it descends upon those who treat any form of life with disrespect and metes out wrathful, ruthless punishment.

entries.name: Sprigatito
entries.desc: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.

entries.name: Floragato
entries.desc: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.

entries.name: Meowscarada
entries.desc: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.

entries.name: Fuecoco
entries.desc: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.

entries.name: Crocalor
entries.desc: The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.

entries.name: Skeledirge
entries.desc: The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.

entries.name: Quaxly
entries.desc: This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.

entries.name: Quaxwell
entries.desc: These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.

entries.name: Quaquaval
entries.desc: A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.

entries.name: Lechonk
entries.desc: It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.

entries.name: Oinkologne
entries.desc: This Pokémon sends a flowerlike scent wafting about. Well-developed muscles in its legs allow it to leap more than 16 feet with no trouble at all.

entries.name: Oinkologne
entries.desc: Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.

entries.name: Tarountula
entries.desc: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.

entries.name: Spidops
entries.desc: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

entries.name: Nymble
entries.desc: It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.

entries.name: Lokix
entries.desc: When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.

entries.name: Pawmi
entries.desc: It has underdeveloped electric sacs on its cheeks. These sacs can produce electricity only if Pawmi rubs them furiously with the pads on its forepaws.

entries.name: Pawmo
entries.desc: When its group is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into battle, defeating enemies with a fighting technique that utilizes electric shocks.

entries.name: Pawmot
entries.desc: This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.

entries.name: Tandemaus
entries.desc: Exhibiting great teamwork, they use their incisors to cut pieces out of any material that might be useful for a nest, then make off with them.

entries.name: Maushold
entries.desc: The two little ones just appeared one day. The group might be a family of related Pokémon, but nobody knows for sure.

entries.name: Maushold
entries.desc: They build huge nests with many rooms that are used for different purposes, such as eating and sleeping.

entries.name: Fidough
entries.desc: This Pokémon is smooth and moist to the touch. Yeast in Fidough’s breath induces fermentation in the Pokémon’s vicinity.

entries.name: Dachsbun
entries.desc: The pleasant aroma that emanates from this Pokémon’s body helps wheat grow, so Dachsbun has been treasured by farming villages.

entries.name: Smoliv
entries.desc: It protects itself from enemies by emitting oil from the fruit on its head. This oil is bitter and astringent enough to make someone flinch.

entries.name: Dolliv
entries.desc: Dolliv shares its tasty, fresh-scented oil with others. This species has coexisted with humans since times long gone.

entries.name: Arboliva
entries.desc: This calm Pokémon is very compassionate. It will share its delicious, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon.

entries.name: Squawkabilly
entries.desc: These Pokémon prefer to live in cities. They form flocks based on the color of their feathers, and they fight over territory.

entries.name: Squawkabilly
entries.desc: The largest of their flocks can contain more than 50 individuals. They fly around towns and forests, searching for food and making a racket.

entries.name: Squawkabilly
entries.desc: These Squawkabilly are hotheaded, and their fighting style is vicious. They’ll leap within reach of their foes to engage in close combat.

entries.name: Squawkabilly
entries.desc: This Pokémon dislikes being alone. It has a strong sense of community and survives by cooperating with allies.

entries.name: Nacli
entries.desc: It was born in a layer of rock salt deep under the earth. This species was particularly treasured in the old days, as they would share precious salt.

entries.name: Naclstack
entries.desc: This Pokémon dry cures its prey by spraying salt over them. The curing process steals away the water in the prey’s body.

entries.name: Garganacl
entries.desc: Garganacl will rub its fingertips together and sprinkle injured Pokémon with salt. Even severe wounds will promptly heal afterward.

entries.name: Charcadet
entries.desc: Burnt charcoal came to life and became a Pokémon. Possessing a fiery fighting spirit, Charcadet will battle even tough opponents.

entries.name: Armarouge
entries.desc: Armarouge evolved through the use of a set of armor that belonged to a distinguished warrior. This Pokémon is incredibly loyal.

entries.name: Ceruledge
entries.desc: The fiery blades on its arms burn fiercely with the lingering resentment of a sword wielder who fell before accomplishing their goal.

entries.name: Tadbulb
entries.desc: Tadbulb shakes its tail to generate electricity. If it senses danger, it will make its head blink on and off to alert its allies.

entries.name: Bellibolt
entries.desc: When this Pokémon expands and contracts its wobbly body, the belly-button dynamo in its stomach produces a huge amount of electricity.

entries.name: Wattrel
entries.desc: When its wings catch the wind, the bones within produce electricity. This Pokémon dives into the ocean, catching prey by electrocuting them.

entries.name: Kilowattrel
entries.desc: Kilowattrel inflates its throat sac to amplify its electricity. By riding the wind, this Pokémon can fly over 430 miles in a day.

entries.name: Maschiff
entries.desc: It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff’s face.

entries.name: Mabosstiff
entries.desc: This Pokémon can store energy in its large dewlap. Mabosstiff unleashes this energy all at once to blow away enemies.

entries.name: Shroodle
entries.desc: Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.

entries.name: Grafaiai
entries.desc: The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.

entries.name: Bramblin
entries.desc: A soul unable to move on to the afterlife was blown around by the wind until it got tangled up with dried grass and became a Pokémon.

entries.name: Brambleghast
entries.desc: It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.

entries.name: Toedscool
entries.desc: Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

entries.name: Toedscruel
entries.desc: These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.

entries.name: Klawf
entries.desc: Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.

entries.name: Capsakid
entries.desc: The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.

entries.name: Scovillain
entries.desc: The red head converts spicy chemicals into fire energy and blasts the surrounding area with a super spicy stream of flame.

entries.name: Rellor
entries.desc: This Pokémon creates a mud ball by mixing sand and dirt with psychic energy. It treasures its mud ball more than its own life.

entries.name: Rabsca
entries.desc: The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.

entries.name: Flittle
entries.desc: Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.

entries.name: Espathra
entries.desc: It immobilizes opponents by bathing them in psychic power from its large eyes. Despite its appearance, it has a vicious temperament.

entries.name: Tinkatink
entries.desc: It swings its handmade hammer around to protect itself, but the hammer is often stolen by Pokémon that eat metal.

entries.name: Tinkatuff
entries.desc: This Pokémon will attack groups of Pawniard and Bisharp, gathering metal from them in order to create a large and sturdy hammer.

entries.name: Tinkaton
entries.desc: This intelligent Pokémon has a very daring disposition. It knocks rocks into the sky with its hammer, aiming for flying Corviknight.

entries.name: Wiglett
entries.desc: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

entries.name: Wugtrio
entries.desc: It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.

entries.name: Bombirdier
entries.desc: It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.

entries.name: Finizen
entries.desc: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

entries.name: Varoom
entries.desc: It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.

entries.name: Revavroom
entries.desc: It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders— now numbering eight—to generate energy.

entries.name: Cyclizar
entries.desc: Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.

entries.name: Orthworm
entries.desc: When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.

entries.name: Glimmet
entries.desc: It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.

entries.name: Glimmora
entries.desc: When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.

entries.name: Greavard
entries.desc: It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.

entries.name: Houndstone
entries.desc: Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.

entries.name: Flamigo
entries.desc: This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.

entries.name: Cetoddle
entries.desc: This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.

entries.name: Cetitan
entries.desc: This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.

entries.name: Veluza
entries.desc: When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.

entries.name: Dondozo
entries.desc: This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.

entries.name: Tatsugiri
entries.desc: This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.

entries.name: Tatsugiri
entries.desc: This species’ differing colors and patterns are apparently the result of Tatsugiri changing itself to suit the preferences of the prey it lures in.

entries.name: Tatsugiri
entries.desc: Bird Pokémon are its main prey. This Pokémon knows it’s weak, so it hunts with a partner.

entries.name: Annihilape
entries.desc: When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.

entries.name: Clodsire
entries.desc: When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.

entries.name: Farigiraf
entries.desc: Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.

entries.name: Dudunsparce
entries.desc: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

entries.name: Dudunsparce
entries.desc: The gentle Dudunsparce will put Pokémon that wander into its nest onto its back and carry them to the entrance.

entries.name: Kingambit
entries.desc: Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.

entries.name: Great Tusk
entries.desc: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

entries.name: Scream Tail
entries.desc: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

entries.name: Brute Bonnet
entries.desc: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

entries.name: Flutter Mane
entries.desc: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

entries.name: Slither Wing
entries.desc: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.

entries.name: Sandy Shocks
entries.desc: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

entries.name: Iron Treads
entries.desc: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

entries.name: Iron Bundle
entries.desc: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

entries.name: Iron Hands
entries.desc: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

entries.name: Iron Jugulis
entries.desc: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

entries.name: Iron Moth
entries.desc: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

entries.name: Iron Thorns
entries.desc: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

entries.name: Frigibax
entries.desc: Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.

entries.name: Arctibax
entries.desc: Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.

entries.name: Baxcalibur
entries.desc: This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.

entries.name: Gimmighoul
entries.desc: This Pokémon was born from passion that seeped into a coin. It wanders, apparently seeking to return to the treasure chest it once inhabited.

entries.name: Gholdengo
entries.desc: Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.

entries.name: Wo-Chien
entries.desc: The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.

entries.name: Chien-Pao
entries.desc: This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.

entries.name: Ting-Lu
entries.desc: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.

entries.name: Chi-Yu
entries.desc: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.

entries.name: Roaring Moon
entries.desc: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

entries.name: Iron Valiant
entries.desc: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.
